events.title: Sneaker on Studio White
must_haves: The same sneaker is shown in its original side view, fully inside the frame.
The sneaker's leather, laces and sole details remain recognizable.
The grey floor and clutter are replaced by a seamless white setting.
A soft shadow beneath the sneaker grounds it without introducing a visible floor boundary.
The image is 16:9 with no added text.

answer_sheet.Which product: The white leather sneaker in product-sneaker.jpg.
answer_sheet.Background: Plain seamless studio white, with no props or visible room.
answer_sheet.Shadow and product preservation: A soft shadow directly underneath; preserve the whole shoe, its side view, leather detail, laces and sole.
answer_sheet.Format and text: One 16:9 image at the standard free size, with no added text.

events.text: Could you make this pic into a clean product shot on plain studio white? I’m hoping it will feel a bit more polished, because I’ve been second-guessing how the current photo looks. Just give it a soft shadow underneath, with no text.

events.text: Credits have run out, so the image generation got blocked. The cheapest model I tried, flux-2-klein, costs 5 credits and was refused, and remove_image_background also costs 5, so it will probably be refused too. I shouldn't keep trying other paid tools; I'll explain the block plainly.

I couldn't make the studio shot. Your Magic Hour account doesn't have enough credits, so it refused the edit. Nothing was created and you weren't charged.

I'd tried the cheapest edit your free plan allows, about 5 credits for one image. Since that was refused, the background-removal tool (also 5 credits) would almost certainly be refused too.

The edit I set up was:
- **Background:** the clutter and grey floor replaced with plain studio white, plus a soft shadow under the shoe
- **Shoe:** the whole sneaker in the same side view and position, with its shape, stitching, laces, heel tab, sole and colour left as they are
- **Shape:** wide (16:9), close to your original
- **Text:** none

**About the shoe looking different:** you're right to worry. AI image editing can slightly change fine details like the stitching, the lace loops or the line of the sole. If you need the shoe to look exactly like the real product, removing the background is safer than a full edit. That tool cuts the shoe out instead of redrawing it, and it can also add a white background. The catch is that it doesn't add a shadow.

**Next step:** once you add credits or a credit pack, tell me which you prefer:
1. **The full edit:** white background with a soft shadow, but small changes to the shoe are possible.
2. **The background removal:** the shoe stays exactly as photographed on plain white, with no shadow.

Your photo is already a clean side view with even light, so either one should give you a polished product shot.

events.why: The edit was refused because the account lacks credits and nothing was created. The reply asks the user to choose between two options, but only after they add credits, so the main message is that it can't do this on the current plan.
